statement: A boolean-only abstention flag conflates a self-imposed, disclosed coverage limit with a genuine read failure (data the tool expected and could not read); a composite denominator that keeps every abstention at a punitive zero then punishes the self-imposed case instead of excluding it like any other measurement gap. Incident: cejel's scorer built its 'read-failure abstentions stay at zero' set from a single insufficientData=true boolean with no reason, so a file skipped only for exceeding the tool's own declared size limit was scored like a file the filesystem refused to read -- both zeroed a criterion into the composite. Fix: carry the reason on the abstention (a reason field, not a bare boolean); an absent reason defaults to the conservative reading (real failure) so no producer changes silently. Rule: when one boolean gap flag can arise from conditions deserving different downstream treatment, attach the reason before they are scored the same way.
